presets.label: raid (two-hander)
why: Deep Wounds turns your crits into bleeds and Impale raises your abilities’ critical damage. Bloodthrill (2/2) gives main-hand swings on your Rend target a 20% chance to enable Overpower, and Improved Overpower makes it likelier to crit.
Improved Tactical Mastery (3/3) keeps up to 15 more Rage when you change stances, Anger Management adds Rage in combat, and Weaponmaster and Two-Handed Weapon Specialization reward your two-hander.
The points freed by the shorter Improved Tactical Mastery and Bloodthrill go to Improved Charge, Reckless Swings (your next 4 melee attacks generate 5 more Rage) and Improved Execute.

presets.label: battlegrounds
why: Mortal Strike’s healing cut, Improved Hamstring’s 15% chance to immobilize and Spearing Strike, which dismounts mounted targets, are the reasons to play Arms in PvP.
Improved Charge adds 6 Rage to your opener, Piercing Howl dazes every enemy within 10 yards, and Iron Will shortens stuns and fears on you by 15%.
Improved Tactical Mastery now stops at three ranks, so its two spare points complete Deflection for 5% parry.

presets.label: leveling to 30
why: Improved Charge adds 6 Rage on the opener, Anger Management adds Rage in combat and slows its loss between pulls, and Improved Tactical Mastery keeps up to 15 more Rage when you swap stances.
Improved Rend opens Deep Wounds, which turns your crits into bleeds, Impale adds critical damage, and Two-Handed Weapon Specialization adds damage with your two-hander.
With Improved Tactical Mastery at three ranks, Impale fills row 4 so the 21st point can still open Bloodthrill at level 30.

presets.label: raid (dual-wield)
why: Dual Wield Specialization, Furious Precision and Flurry (3/3: 30% faster swings for 3 attacks after a melee crit) keep both weapons busy, with Cruelty and Unbridled Wrath for crit and Rage.
Death Wish leads to Bloodthirst, and Flurry no longer needs Death Wish. Reckless Swings and Improved Whirlwind, new in Fury, add Rage and a faster, harder Whirlwind.
Eleven Arms points take Improved Heroic Strike, Deflection, Improved Charge, Improved Tactical Mastery and Anger Management. Raging Blows is no longer in the tree.

presets.label: leveling to 30 (dual-wield)
why: Cruelty and Unbridled Wrath come first for melee crit and a chance of extra Rage on every weapon hit.
Furious Precision and Dual Wield Specialization make the off-hand land more often and hit harder, and Blood Craze heals you after you take a crit or a big hit.
Death Wish at level 30 helps on tough pulls and later leads to Bloodthirst. Flurry no longer depends on it.

presets.label: raid tank
why: Shield Specialization and Master of Defense turn blocks, dodges and parries into Rage, Deflection adds 5% parry to feed that, and Anticipation adds Defense.

Improved Thunder Clap, Improved Sunder Armor and Focused Rage make threat abilities cheaper, Defiance and Bastion add threat and damage while you wear a shield, and Vanguard lets you Charge in Defensive Stance.
Improved Tactical Mastery now has three ranks, so two Arms points go to Improved Charge and Anger Management stays in reach.

presets.label: dungeon tank to 30
why: Shield Specialization and Master of Defense give Rage when you block, dodge or parry, and Improved Bloodrage raises the Rage from Bloodrage (25% at rank 1).
Improved Thunder Clap and Defiance help you hold packs in early dungeons, and Improved Sunder Armor makes Sunder cheaper.
Vanguard lets you open with Charge without leaving Defensive Stance.
